title: Finite polynomial extension and contraction along the zero section
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\beta:R\to S$ a finite ring homomorphism, and $\mathfrak p\subset S$ an ideal. Finite means that $S$ is generated by a finite list $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ as an $R$-module through $\beta$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $\widetilde\beta:R[Z]\to S[T]$ for the coefficientwise extension with $Z\mapsto T$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then the same constants $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ generate $S[T]$ as an $R[Z]$-module, so $\widetilde\beta$ is finite, and $$\widetilde\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak pS[T]+(T))=\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p)R[Z]+(Z).$$ Equivalently, for every $H\in R[Z]$, $\widetilde\beta(H)\in\mathfrak pS[T]+(T)$ if and only if $\beta(H(0))\in\mathfrak p$. In particular, if $k$ is a field, $m\ge0$, $R=k[z_1,\ldots,z_m]$, $S=k[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, $\beta$ is a finite $k$-algebra map and $\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=(z_{r+1},\ldots,z_m)$ for some $0\le r\le m$, then the $k$-algebra extension $z_{m+1}\mapsto y_{m+1}$ has contraction $(z_{r+1},\ldots,z_m,z_{m+1})$ of $\mathfrak pS[y_{m+1}]+(y_{m+1})$. The formula holds for nonprime ideals, noninjective maps, zero rings, and empty finite generating lists as well.

proof.text: Write $C_A:A\to A[U]$ for constant polynomials. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $\widetilde\beta(\sum_i a_iZ^i)=\sum_i\beta(a_i)T^i$, and this is a ring map: addition is coefficientwise and each coefficient of a product is a finite sum of products of coefficients. For $F=\sum_{i=0}^N s_iT^i$, choose $a_{ij}\in R$ with $s_i=\sum_{j=1}^s\beta(a_{ij})b_j$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $F=\sum_{j=1}^s\widetilde\beta(\sum_{i=0}^N a_{ij}Z^i)C_S(b_j)$ by comparing coefficients. Thus the specified constants generate over $R[Z]$ and the map is finite.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $A$, ideal $I\subset A$, and $P=\sum_{i=0}^N c_iU^i$, put $Q=\sum_{i=1}^N c_iU^{i-1}$. The coefficient identity $P=C_A(c_0)+UQ$ implies $P\in IA[U]+(U)$ whenever $P(0)=c_0\in I$. Conversely an element of that ideal is a finite sum $\sum_\ell C_A(a_\ell)V_\ell+UW$ with $a_\ell\in I$; its value at zero is $\sum_\ell a_\ell V_\ell(0)\in I$. Hence membership is equivalent to $P(0)\in I$. This uses only finite polynomial expansion and the definition of the ideal generated by the displayed elements.

proof.text: For $H=\sum_i h_iZ^i$, the coefficient formula in step 1 gives $\widetilde\beta(H)(0)=\beta(h_0)=\beta(H(0))$. Apply step 2 first with $(A,I)=(S,\mathfrak p)$ and then with $(A,I)=(R,\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p))$. It gives $\widetilde\beta(H)\in\mathfrak pS[T]+(T)$ if and only if $\beta(H(0))\in\mathfrak p$, if and only if $H\in\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p)R[Z]+(Z)$. Equality of the ideals follows element by element.

source.place: Tag 051P (lemma-refined-Noether-normalization), proof: extension by z_n mapping to y_n and final contraction; explicit elementary details supplied by NC.

proof.text: In the stated $k$-algebra case, group each monomial by its exponent of the last variable to identify $k[z_1,\ldots,z_{m+1}]=R[Z]$ and $k[y_1,\ldots,y_{m+1}]=S[T]$, with $Z=z_{m+1}$ and $T=y_{m+1}$. The coefficient extension fixes $k$ and sends $Z$ to $T$. Substitute $\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=(z_{r+1},\ldots,z_m)$ into step 3; extending an ideal generated by these elements simply allows polynomial multipliers, so adjoining $(Z)$ gives $(z_{r+1},\ldots,z_m,z_{m+1})$. When $m=0$ or $r=m$ the indicated old variable list is empty. No argument used primality or injectivity. If $s=0$, the generating hypothesis says every element of $S$ is zero, and all finite sums and identities above still hold in its zero polynomial ring.

lean.statement: theorem finite_mapRingHom_and_comap_zero_section {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (β : R →+* S) (hβ : β.Finite) (p : Ideal S) : (∀ (s : ℕ) (b : Fin s → S), (∀ y : S, ∃ a : Fin s → R, ∑ j, β (a j) * b j = y) → ∀ F : Polynomial S, ∃ A : Fin s → Polynomial R, ∑ j, mapRingHom β (A j) * C (b j) = F) ∧ (mapRingHom β).Finite ∧ Ideal.comap (mapRingHom β) (Ideal.map C p ⊔ Ideal.span {X}) = Ideal.map C (Ideal.comap β p) ⊔ Ideal.span {X} ∧ (∀ H : Polynomial R, mapRingHom β H ∈ Ideal.map C p ⊔ Ideal.span {X} ↔ β (H.eval 0) ∈ p)
lean.note: The first declaration states the general ring-map calculation, including the same finite generating lists; the second states the k-algebra coordinate specialization on the canonically identical iterated polynomial rings, using the outer X as the new last variable.
